summary: Iteration 47 — Admin-managed Biblioteca folders + content assignment + user Biblioteca grouped by folder + Home section rename. Backend: 8/8 pytest passing (/app/backend/tests/test_library_folders.py → /app/test_reports/pytest/iteration_47_library_folders.xml) — public GET /api/library-folders returns seeded defaults sorted by order (Podcast/Meditazioni/Studi Biblici/Predicazioni/Video/Programmi), admin CRUD /api/admin/library-folders create/rename/reorder/delete works, GET /api/admin/content-catalog returns items per type with folder_id, POST /api/admin/content-folder assigns and toggles-off, GET /api/me/library groups favorites into the admin folders (default_types mapping for meditazioni→Meditazioni and explicit assignment reflects immediately). Frontend (mobile 390x844): (1) Admin '/admin/library-folders' — seeded folders render as cards, 'create-folder' with 'new-folder-name' creates a new folder (verified via API), 'folder-name-<id>' + 'save-folder-<id>' rename persists, 'delete-folder-<id>' triggers a confirm and deletes (via UI clicks; test used dialog=accept), and the reorder chevron-down inside the first folder card successfully bubbled up 5 PUTs that reassigned orders 0..N (Podcast moved to order 1, Meditazioni to 0). (2) Admin '/admin/content-folders' — all 6 type sections render with chip rows, tapping testID assign-<itemId>-<folderId> assigns and tapping again removes (both persist via API check). (3) User /biblioteca — after favoriting a meditation and a studi-biblici, only the two matching folders render (testID lib-folder-<folderId>); opening the Meditazioni folder shows folder-item-<med_id> with folder-remove-<id>, tapping remove unfavorites correctly (verified via /api/me/content-fav-ids). (4) Reassignment effect — assigning meditazioni to Studi Biblici folder puts the item into that folder group in /me/library. (5) Home section rename — setting section_labels.home_podcast → 'PodcastRenamedIter47' via PUT /api/admin/settings renders on Home instead of 'Ultimi Podcast'. (6) Regression — Home + bottom nav render, Biblioteca ↔ folder detail navigation stable, no red screen, only pre-existing RN-Web shadow*/textShadow* warnings (unrelated). BACKEND BUG FOUND AND FIXED: `FolderIn` Pydantic model in /app/backend/server.py had `name: str` as required, breaking partial-update PUTs used by the admin UI for reorder and icon change (frontend sends only {order} or {icon}). I split it into two models: FolderIn (all optional, used by PUT) and FolderCreateIn (name required, used by POST). Verified fix with curl (before: 422 'name required'; after: 200 ok) and via UI chevron reorder click.

rca_of_issue: RCA (backend bug found & fixed): FolderIn was reused for both POST (create) and PUT (partial update) — but declared `name: str` as required. FastAPI/Pydantic returned 422 for any PUT missing 'name'. The admin UI move()/setIcon() calls send only {order} / {icon} and wrap the request in `.catch(()=>{})`, so failures were silently swallowed — reorder & icon-change appeared broken to the admin. Fix: split into two models — FolderIn (all optional, PUT) + FolderCreateIn (name required, POST). Verified via curl and UI: reorder chevron and icon chip now persist. Mitigation for future: don't reuse creation schemas for partial updates; either use `PartialFolderIn` or leverage `Field(...)` + `exclude_unset=True` with all-optional fields.
